chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Say, O Allah! I ask You for the words of the repentants and their deeds, and the light of the Prophets and their truthfulness, and the salvation of the Mujahideen and their reward, and the gratitude of the Chosen ones and their advice, and the deeds of the Rememberers and their conviction, and the faith of the scholars and their understanding, and the worship of the humble ones and their humility, and the wisdom of the jurists and their conduct, and the fear of the pious and their desire, and the affirmation of the believers and their reliance, and the hope of the good-doers and their righteousness.
O Allah! I ask You for the reward of the grateful, and the station of the near ones, and the companionship of the Prophets.

O Allah! I ask You for the fear of those who work for You, and the deeds of those who fear You, and the humility of those who worship You, worship You, and the conviction of those who rely upon You, and the reliance of the believers in You.

O Allah! You are Knowing of my need without being taught, and You are Capacious for it without being strained. You are the One whom no beggar exhausts, and no attainer diminishes, and no speaker's words can reach Your praise. You are as You say, and above what we say.
O Allah! Make for me a relief that is near, and a great reward, and a beautiful covering.
O Allah! You know that I am upon injustice to myself and extravagance upon it, and I have not taken for You an opposite, nor a match, nor a companion, nor a son.

O He whom questions do not confuse, O He whom nothing occupies from anything, nor hearing from hearing, nor sight from sight, and whom the insistence of the insistent does not tire. I ask You to relieve me in this hour of mine from where I expect and from where I do not expect. You revive the bones when they are dust, and You are Able over all things.

O He to whom my little gratitude did not deprive me, and my great sin did not expose me, and He saw me upon disobedience but did not confront me, and He created me for what He created me for, but I did other than what He created me for. So what a good Master You are, O my Master, and what an evil servant I am. You found me, and what a good Seeker You are, O my Lord, and what an evil sought one I am. You found me Your servant, and the son of Your servant, and the son of Your maid, before You. Do with me what You will.

O Allah! The voices have subsided, and the movements have settled, and every beloved is alone with his beloved, and I am alone with You, You are the Beloved to me. So make my solitude with You tonight the emancipation from the Fire.

O He whom no describer describes above Him, O He whom no creature has a barrier besides Him. O the First before all things, and O the Last after all things. O He who has no element, and O He whose End does not perish. O the Most Perfect of the Described, and O the Most Generous of the Givers. O He who understands every language by which He is called, and O He whose Pardoning is ancient, and His Grip is severe, and His Kingdom is upright.
I ask You by Your Name which You spoke to Musa, O Allah, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O He whom there is no god except You. O Allah! You are the Self-Sufficient.
I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to admit me into Paradise by Your Mercy.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for all needs in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This supplication, known as *Dua al-Hajah*, is a cornerstone of Shia devotional practice, often recited for general needs (*kashifat al-karaj*). It structurally moves from invoking the spiritual stations of the righteous to affirming Allah’s absolute sufficiency (*Al-Samad*) and mercy, culminating in a humble admission of human frailty and reliance on divine grace. Scholars highlight its comprehensive nature, blending theological affirmation with practical intercession for both worldly relief and hereafter success.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Say, ‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj for the words of the repentants and their deeds, and Light of the Prophetsas and theiras truthfulness, and the salvation of the Mujahideen (soldiers) and their Rewards, and the gratefulness of the Chosen ones and their advice, and the deeds of the Zakireen (Oft-mentioners of Allahazwj) and their conviction, and Eman of the scholar and their understanding, and the worship of the fearful ones and their humbleness, and wisdom of the jurists and their ways, and fear of the pious ones and their wishes, and the ratification of the Momineen and their reliance (upon Allahazwj), and hopes of the good doers and their righteousness.
O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the Rewards of the grateful ones, and the status of the ones of Proximity, and the friendship of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> for the fear of the workers for You<sup>azwj</sup>, and the deeds of the ones fearful from You<sup>azwj</sup>, and the humbleness of the worshippers to You<sup>azwj</sup>, and the conviction of the ones relying upon You<sup>azwj</sup>, and the reliance of the Momineen with You<sup>azwj</sup>.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> are Knowing of my needs without these being made known, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are Capacious for these without any encumberance, and You<sup>azwj</sup> are such that no beggar can Exhaust You<sup>azwj</sup>, and not attainer can reduce You<sup>azwj</sup> (of Your<sup>azwj</sup> resources), and no word of a speaker can reach Your<sup>azwj</sup> (Rightful) Praise. You<sup>azwj</sup> are just as You<sup>azwj</sup> are Saying, and above what we are saying.
O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Make a relief for me to be close-by, and a great Recompense, and a beautiful Veiling.

O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> Know that I am upon doing injustice to myself, and my extravagance upon it. I have neither taken to be for You<sup>azwj</sup>, an opposite, nor a match, nor a female companion nor a son.

O the One Whom the questions do make Him<sup>azwj</sup> to err! O the One Whom nothing can pre-occupy from anything, nor a hearing from Hearing, nor a sight from Seeing, nor does the insistence of the insisting ones Tire Him<sup>azwj</sup>. I Ask You<sup>azwj</sup> that You<sup>azwj</sup> Relieve from me during this time of mine, from where I an expecting and from where I am not expecting. You<sup>azwj</sup> will Revive the bones when they are dust, and You are Able upon every thing.

O the One Who received little thanks of mine but did not Deprive me, and grievous were my sins but did not Expose me, and Saw me to be upon the disobedience but did not Confront me, and Created me for which I was Created for, but I did other than what I was Created for. So the Best Master are You<sup>azwj</sup>, O my Master, and the most evil worshipper am I. You<sup>azwj</sup> Found me and the Best Seeker are You<sup>azwj</sup>my Lord<sup>azwj</sup> and the most evil of the sought ones am I, as You<sup>azwj</sup> Know me, I am Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant, and son of Your<sup>azwj</sup> servant, and son of Your<sup>azwj</sup> maid, in front of You<sup>azwj</sup>. Do whatever You<sup>azwj</sup> so Desire to with me.

O Allahazwj! The voices have subsided, and the movements have settled, and every beloved is alone with his beloved, and Youazwj are Alone with me. Youazwj are the Beloved to me, therefore Make my being Alone with Youazwj at night to be an Emancipation from the Fire.

O the One Who, there is none above Him<sup>azwj</sup> to describe for the Knowledge! O the One Who, there is no Defender for the creatures besides Him<sup>azwj</sup>! O the First One before everything, and O the last One after everything! O the One Who there are no ingredients for Him<sup>azwj</sup>! O the One Who there is no perishing for His<sup>azwj</sup> End, and O the One of Complete Attributes, and O Pardoner of the obeying ones, and O the One Who Surpasses with every language supplicated with, and O the One Whose Pardoning is ancient, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Grip is intense, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Kingdom is straight.

I ask You<sup>azwj</sup> by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Name Which You<sup>azwj</sup> Faced Musa<sup>as</sup> with, O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, O Beneficent, O Merciful! There is no god except You<sup>azwj</sup>. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Last.
I ask Youazwj that Youazwj Send Salawāt upon Muhammadsaww and the Progenyasws of Muhammadsaww, and that Youazwj Enter me into the Paradise by Yourazwj Mercy’.
en.sarwar: 33. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunus from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Say, ‘O Lord, I plead before You, to grant me such words as those of repenting people and their deeds, the light of the prophets and their truthfulness, salvation of the fighters for Your cause and their rewards, thankfulness of the chosen ones and their good advice, actions of those who speak of You and their certainty, belief of the scholars and their deep understanding, worship of the concerned people and their humility, the judgment of the experts in the law (Shari’ a) and their discipline, worries of the pious people and their interest (in religion), the affirmation of the believing people and their trusting (Allah) and the hope of the virtuous people and their good deeds.
“O Lord, I plead before You grant me a reward as that granted to those who thank (You), the position of those very near to (You) and the friendship of the prophets.

O Lord, I plead before You to grant me a fear like that of the people who act for Your sake, the acts of those who fear You, the humility of those who worship You, the certainty of those who place their trust in You and the trust of the believing people with You.

O Lord, You know my needs without being taught, and You are capable of helping without being burdened. You are the One Whom no pleading person can overcome verbally, or anyone can find faults with or anyone can exhaust His praise. O Lord, You are as You say and above what we say.
O Lord, provide me immediate relief, great rewards, and beautiful covering.
O Lord, You know that in doing injustice to myself and transgressing against it I did not take anyone as Your opposition, partner, companion, or a child.

“O the One whom pleading cannot confuse, nothing can preoccupy in listening to one from listening to the other, seeing one from seeing the other and the insistence of insisting people cannot tire Him. I plead before You to provide me relief in this hour from the sources I except or from that which I do not expect; You bring to life the bones that have turned to ashes; You have power over all things.

O the One to whom my thanks had been very little but He has not deprived me, my sins were monstrous but He has not disgraced me. He found me in sins but did not encounter me. He created me for what He has created me but I have acted against what He has created me for. What a great owner are You O my Master! What a despicable slave am I! You have found me, You are the best of finders O Lord! What a despicable thing am 1 to look for! It is Your slave, the son of Your slave and the son of Your female slave before You to deal with as You will.

O Lord, the voices have silenced, movements have calmed down, every loving one has sought privacy with his beloved, and I have sought privacy with You. You are the beloved to me, make the privacy that 1 have sought with You my freedom from the fire.

O the One above whom there is no person of knowledge more praiseworthy. O the One below whom there is no creature barred to reach Him. O the First before all things, O the Last after all things. O the One who has no elements, O the One for whom there is no end for annihilation, O the One of perfect attributes, O the most lenient of providers, O the One who communicates with all languages and is spoken to as well, O the One whose forgiveness had been there from long before, whose hold is stern, whose kingdom is solid,
I plead before You through Your name with which You faced Moses, O Allah, O the Beneficent, O the Merciful, O the One, no one deserves to be worshipped except You. O Lord, You are Selfsufficient,
I plead before You to bestow al-Salat (favors) upon Muhammad and his family and admit me in paradise.”
